Spring Herb and Feta Frittata

Served at: Spring Equinox (Ostara)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 25 min

This vibrant Spring Herb and Feta Frittata celebrates the fresh growth of Ostara, the Spring Equinox. Bursting with the flavors of new herbs and rich eggs, it's a perfect dish to welcome the season's renewal and share with loved ones during a celebratory brunch or light meal.

Ingredients

  • 8 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk or cream
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 small shallot, finely chopped
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 1 cup (25g) fresh spinach, roughly chopped
  • 1/4 cup (6g) chopped fresh parsley
  • 1/4 cup (6g) chopped fresh chives
  • 2 tablespoons (3g) chopped fresh dill
  • 2 tablespoons (3g) chopped fresh mint
  • 1/2 cup (60g) crumbled feta cheese
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk or cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper until well combined and slightly frothy.
  3. Heat the olive oil in a 10-inch (25 cm) oven-safe, non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped shallot and cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
  4. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  5. Stir in the chopped spinach and cook until just wilted, about 1-2 minutes. Remove the skillet from the heat.
  6. Gently stir in the fresh parsley, chives, dill, and mint into the egg mixture.
  7. Pour the egg and herb mixture evenly over the vegetables in the skillet. Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese over the top.
  8. Cook on the stovetop over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, or until the edges begin to set and pull away from the sides of the pan.
  9. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 15-18 minutes, or until the frittata is puffed and set in the center.
  10. Let the frittata rest for 5 minutes before slicing into wedges and serving.

Tips

  • Feel free to experiment with other spring herbs like tarragon or basil.
  • For added texture, you can include thinly sliced asparagus or green onions.
  • Serve warm or at room temperature, perhaps with a side of crusty bread or a light green salad.
